extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and commenters (scientists, public water systems, regulated entities, researchers, and the general public) preparing comments on the EPA's draft Contaminant Candidate List 6 (CCL 6)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit public comments and technical input in response to the EPA's Draft Sixth Contaminant Candidate List (CCL 6), addressing the list contents, data sources, screening/classification methods, grouping decisions, and identified data needs. The page describes statutory requirements, EPA screening/classification methods, requested comment topics, and submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory CCL listing requirements (SDWA §1412(b)(1)(B)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The list must include contaminants that are not subject to any proposed or promulgated National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (NPDWRs), are known or anticipated to occur in public water systems (PWSs), and may require regulation under the Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute also provides that unregulated contaminants considered shall include, but not be limited to, hazardous substances identified in CERCLA section 101(14) and substances registered as pesticides under FIFRA. In selecting contaminants, EPA must consider human health effects on sensitive subgroups (infants, children, pregnant women, elderly, individuals with serious illness, and other identifiable higher-risk subpopulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory criteria for regulatory determinations (SDWA §1412(b)(1)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a regulatory determination on a CCL contaminant, EPA must evaluate whether: (1) the contaminant may have an adverse effect on the health of persons; (2) the contaminant is known to occur or there is a substantial likelihood it will occur in public water systems with a frequency and at levels of public health concern; and (3) in the Administrator's sole judgment, regulation of the contaminant presents a meaningful opportunity for health risk reduction for persons served by PWSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive regulatory determination results in rulemaking for an NPDWR; at least five CCL contaminants must have regulatory determinations every five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and use of the CCL
rubrics_metrics.description: The CCL is the initial screening step in the SDWA regulatory framework to identify contaminants that may require regulation and to prioritize research and data collection efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion on the CCL (individual or group) does not itself impose regulatory requirements or mean a contaminant will necessarily be regulated; contaminants with sufficient health and occurrence information are considered for regulatory determination and potential rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source assessment factors for building candidate universes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assessed potential data sources based on four assessment factors: relevancy, completeness, redundancy, and retrievability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors were applied when compiling health and occurrence data sources used to build the Chemical and Microbial Universes; detailed sources and assessments are in the Technical Support Documents (TSDs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical Universe compilation approach
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA compiled a broad Chemical Universe from previous CCLs, Science Advisory Board (SAB) input, and literature searches, identifying thousands of chemicals and many data sources (e.g., 20 health sources and 41 occurrence sources for CCL 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chemical Universe (25,305 chemicals for CCL 6) is the starting pool for screening and prioritization; full methods and data source lists are in the Chemical Technical Support Document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points-based screening for chemicals to create the PCCL
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA applied a points-based screening system that assigned cumulative points to contaminants across health effects and occurrence data elements to determine which chemicals advance to the Preliminary Contaminant Candidate List (PCCL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening scores were used along with statistical models and analyses to prioritize chemicals; scoring details are in Section 3.2 and Section 4.6 of the Chemical Technical Support Document. The result informed selection of top-scoring chemicals for the PCCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for excluding chemicals from the PCCL
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemicals may be excluded from the PCCL for reasons including recent regulatory determinations or pending Agency action, canceled pesticides with no reported alternative uses and rapid environmental breakdown, or because they are part of chemical groups the Agency determined to list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: EPA excluded nine chemicals due to recent regulatory determinations and 25 canceled pesticides from CCL 6 PCCL; exclusions related to group inclusion (DBP, pharmaceutical, PFAS) were applied as described in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification process using Contaminant Information Sheets (CIS) and chemical evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: In classification, EPA compiled main and supplemental data into Contaminant Information Sheets (CIS) for each chemical; 'chemical evaluators' reviewed CIS health effects and occurrence metrics to recommend listing decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental health data were used to calculate health concentrations (non-regulatory health-based toxicity values). EPA compares occurrence data to health concentrations to characterize the likelihood a contaminant may be in drinking water at levels of health concern. Details are in the Chemical Technical Support Document (Sections 4.2, 4.5, 4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation team consensus listing recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical evaluation teams reviewed CISs and provided consensus listing recommendations for PCCL chemicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA validated selection of top-scoring chemicals and the screening framework using statistical modeling. An additional refinement step was used for chemicals with prior negative regulatory determinations to reassess new information since the original decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and criteria for listing chemical groups (DBPs, microplastics, PFAS, pharmaceuticals)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed listing four chemical groups on the draft CCL 6—disinfection byproducts (DBPs), microplastics, PFAS, and pharmaceuticals—recognizing them as Agency priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing a group does not mean EPA will necessarily make regulatory decisions for the entire group; EPA will evaluate scientific data on groups, subgroups, and individual contaminants to inform any regulatory determinations. Examples: DBP group composition, PFAS structural definition, pharmaceutical inclusion criteria (see other rubric entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Microplastics research/data needs for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA identified significant data gaps for microplastics that require further research before fully understanding drinking-water risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key data gaps include: (1) a health-based definition (characteristics like color, polymer, shape, size associated with adverse effects); (2) validated detection technology with quality control, accuracy, precision; (3) understanding microplastics combined with other substances and implications for detection and health risks; (4) better understanding of sources contributing to microplastics in drinking water. Research would also help standardize data collection and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS structural definition for inclusion on CCL
rubrics_metrics.description: For CCL purposes EPA uses the PFAS structural definition adopted for CCL 5 and applied to include PFAS that meet one of three structural patterns (with exclusions for PFAS already subject to national drinking water regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three structures specified in the document (R-(CF2)-CF(R′)R′′; R-CF2OCF2-R′; CF3C(CF3)RR′) are used to identify PFAS for the group listing. Because >4,000 PFAS exist and data are scarce for many, group listing is used to prioritize research rather than evaluate each PFAS individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceuticals inclusion criteria and use of Human Health Benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposes a pharmaceuticals group and considers pharmaceuticals to include any substance defined as a 'drug' under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (1938).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA incorporated new occurrence and health data sources and applied the Human Health Benchmarks for Pharmaceuticals (HHB-Rx) — non-enforceable drinking water levels indicating potential adverse health effects — to inform screening of pharmaceuticals and identification of top-scoring pharmaceutical candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microbial Universe definition and microbial screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The CCL Microbial Universe is defined as microbial contaminants known to cause human disease. Screening criteria narrow the Microbial Universe to pathogens that have potential to be transmitted through drinking water, restricting the microbial PCCL to human pathogens that may cause drinking water-related disease via ingestion, inhalation, or dermal contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any pathogen documented to cause disease transmitted through drinking water, regardless of screening criteria, is also considered for the PCCL. The full Microbial Universe and screening criteria details are in the Microbial Technical Support Document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microbial scoring protocols and selection emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA scored PCCL microbial contaminants using protocols that consider waterborne disease outbreaks, occurrence, and health risks; selection emphasized PCCL microbes with confirmed outbreaks in U.S. public water systems during the evaluated timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three protocols are used and combined to assign numerical values; details on scoring methods and combination procedures are in Chapter 4 of the Microbial Technical Support Document. Prioritization favors pathogens that provide best opportunities to advance public health protection through potential regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of data needs for CCL contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA categorizes chemicals and microbial contaminants into four groups depending upon the availability of occurrence data and health assessments to identify research and information needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These summary tables (Chapter 5 of Chemical TSD and Chapter 6 of Microbial TSD) are intended to communicate research priorities and gaps needed for any future regulatory determinations under SDWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation submission rules and confidentiality guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must include the docket ID (EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0946) and may be submitted via Regulations.gov (preferred), mail, or hand delivery. Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or otherwise restricted. Multimedia submissions must be accompanied by a written comment (the written comment is the official comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may publish comments to the public docket and may redact or withhold certain submissions. EPA generally will not consider comments or contents located outside the primary submission (e.g., on external web/cloud file-sharing systems). For additional submission methods and full EPA public comment policy see EPA docketing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on preparing effective comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested helpful elements for comments: explain views clearly; describe assumptions used; provide technical information, alternative scientific analyses, and/or supporting data; provide full references for any peer-reviewed publications used; provide specific examples to illustrate concerns; offer alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also ensure comments are submitted by the deadline, identify the docket ID number and provide the name, date, and Federal Register citation related to the comments to ensure proper receipt and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between the CCL and the Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CCL informs selection of contaminants for the UCMR; the UCMR (issued once every five years) provides nationally representative occurrence data for up to 30 unregulated contaminants monitored by public water systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occurrence data collected under UCMR can inform future CCLs and regulatory determinations; EPA considers CCL contaminants when selecting UCMR contaminants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and expectation to consult Technical Support Documents and docket materials
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides Technical Support Documents (Chemical, Microbial, and Contaminant Information Sheets) and docket materials (nominations, supporting information) to document methods, data sources, scoring, and selection decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters are invited to review the TSDs and the docket at Regulations.gov (Docket ID EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0946) when submitting comments on data sources, screening/classification processes, listing decisions, and data needs; details and section references to the TSDs are provided throughout the Federal Register notice.
